title: Browser Automation with Stagehand: Finding Company Press Release Pages
summary: Collier King shows how Stagehand combines natural language and code to automate a browser, including a case study that finds company press release pages.
learn: Stagehand has four core calls, observe, act, extract and agent, and the TypeScript project builds on Playwright.
King shows extract with a Zod schema that pulls a product name, price and stock status from a page.
Stagehand can cache the steps an LLM took for act and agent under a custom key, and King says to recompute and cache again when the page changes.
King recommends describing elements ("the sign-in button") instead of how they look ("the blue button"), and not combining multiple steps in one act call.
In the case study, King finds news and PR pages for the Dow 30 companies in three steps: a DuckDuckGo search, clicking around the homepage, then the site search box.
King compares several models, including an open model run on Ollama, and says cheap, older models handle the task, with Haiku the fastest and GPT-4o using the fewest tokens.
